original_question: For the many asymptotically locally conical G2-manifolds that are close to a degenerate Calabi-Yau cone limit and are typically only U(1)-invariant, can one construct G2-instantons that are correspondingly close, in an appropriate sense, to Calabi-Yau monopoles on the limiting cone?
target_in_paper: §4.4(b), the open problem asking whether one can construct G2-instantons on ALC G2-manifolds near the degenerate Calabi–Yau cone limit—typically with only U(1)-symmetry—that are close to Calabi–Yau monopoles on the cone. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the correct part of the paper and is very close to the authors’ wording: it has the right geometric setting (ALC G2-manifolds close to a degenerate Calabi–Yau cone limit), the right symmetry expectation (typically only U(1)), and the right gauge-theoretic target (G2-instantons related to Calabi–Yau monopoles on the cone). This is exactly the motivation expressed in §4.4(b), and Proposition 9 is the nearby precise statement explaining why Calabi–Yau monopoles are the relevant limiting objects. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))
missing_details: The exact target is not a theorem or conjecture but the specific open problem in §4.4(b). ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))

The ambient geometry should be stated using the paper’s ALC setup: outside a compact set K, there is a diffeomorphism p:(1,∞)×Σ→X\K, where π:Σ→Γ is a U(1)-bundle, and ϕ is asymptotic to a U(1)-invariant model ϕ∞ whose metric is dr^2 + m^2 η∞^2 + r^2 π^*g5. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))

The cone in question is not arbitrary: by Proposition 8(a), g5 comes from a Sasaki–Einstein SU(2)-structure on Γ, so the base determines a Calabi–Yau cone (1,∞)×Γ. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))

The paper’s only nearby precise interpretation of being close to a monopole is the asymptotic model used in Proposition 9: there should exist a U(1)-invariant connection A∞ = a + mΦ⊗η∞ on the end with p^*F_A asymptotic at infinity to F_A∞. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))

The limiting object should be identified explicitly as a Calabi–Yau monopole pair (a,Φ), meaning it satisfies Fa∧Ω2 = -(1/2) d_aΦ∧ω^2 and Fa∧ω^2 = 0 on the cone equipped with its conical torsion-free SU(3)-structure (ω,Ω2). ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))

Your draft does not distinguish between the paper’s statement that the underlying ALC examples are typically only U(1)-invariant and the separate Proposition 9 hypothesis that the asymptotic model connection A∞ is U(1)-invariant. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))

The paper does not fix a structure group, bundle topology, norm, or rate for the closeness in §4.4(b); a faithful rewrite should therefore avoid adding such extra hypotheses beyond the asymptotic framework supplied by Proposition 9. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))
refined_question: Let (X,ϕ) be an asymptotically locally conical holonomy G2-manifold of the kind highlighted in §4.4(b), namely one that is close to a degenerate Calabi–Yau cone limit and typically has only U(1)-symmetry. Writing the ALC end as p:(1,∞)×Σ→X\K, where π:Σ→Γ is a U(1)-bundle and the end determines a Calabi–Yau cone (1,∞)×Γ, can one construct a G2-instanton A on a principal bundle over X such that on the end there exists a U(1)-invariant connection A∞ = a + mΦ⊗η∞ with p^*F_A asymptotic at infinity to F_A∞, so that the limiting pair (a,Φ) is a Calabi–Yau monopole on the cone, i.e. Fa∧Ω2 = -(1/2) d_aΦ∧ω^2 and Fa∧ω^2 = 0? ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))
justification: The draft is aimed at the ALC open-problem section, not at the earlier AC results: §4.4(b) says almost verbatim that many ALC G2-manifolds close to the degenerate Calabi–Yau cone limit, typically only U(1)-invariant, should be used to try to construct G2-instantons close to Calabi–Yau monopoles on the cone. The nearby mathematical content that makes this stand-alone is §4.1, which defines the ALC end and identifies its cone as Calabi–Yau via Proposition 8(a), together with §4.2/Proposition 9, which gives the paper’s precise asymptotic relation between a G2-instanton on the ALC end and a Calabi–Yau monopole on the cone. The refined question therefore sharpens only the notion of limit/close by using Proposition 9 and does not broaden the problem beyond the paper. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))
